title: KVCache + Batching Safety-Margin Sensitivity Audit: latency vs quality tail analysis
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Run a focused sensitivity audit that measures the impact of conservative vs aggressive KV cache and batching safety margins on both latency tail behavior (p95/p99/p999) and generation quality. The motivation: recent configs that increase batch sizes and relax cache revalidation reduce average cost but we have sporadic high-latency outliers and small quality regressions on long-context prompts. This ticket scopes experiments, monitoring hooks, and a rollout-safe gating policy for config changes that trade latency for marginal quality shifts.
acceptance_criteria: Define an automated eval harness that runs N=10k representative requests across the prompt corpus (mix of short, medium, long contexts) and reports p50/p95/p99/p999 latency and token-level quality metrics (exact-match/ROUGE-L/human-flavored coherence score).

Produce a latency-quality frontier charts for at least 5 safety-margin settings (e.g., safety=0.0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0) and identify knee points where cost savings disproportionately increase tail latency or drop quality beyond thresholds.

Ship monitoring alerts and a lightweight regression detector that flags >2% relative degradation in the chosen quality composite or >30% increase in p99 latency compared to baseline config, with a clear rollback playbook.
Create a canary rollout recipe (1% -> 10% -> 100%) tied to the regression detector and add the new gating policy to runtime-configs/common/batching.yaml.
Document results and recommendations in Confluence and attach charts/CSV used for decision-making.
